module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Divisibility of $2^n + 1$ by $n$

A56777 lists composite numbers $n$ satisfying both $\varphi(n+12) = \varphi(n) + 12$ and
$\sigma(n+12) = \sigma(n) + 12$.

The conjectures state identities connecting A56777 and prime quadruples (A7530), as
well as congruences satisfied by the members of A56777.

*References:*
- [A56777](https://oeis.org/A56777)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA56777

open Nat
open scoped ArithmeticFunction.sigma

/-- A composite number $n$ is in the sequence A56777 if it satisfies both
$\varphi(n+12) = \varphi(n) + 12$ and $\sigma(n+12) = \sigma(n) + 12$. -/
def A (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ¬n.Prime ∧ 1 < n ∧ totient (n + 12) = totient n + 12 ∧ σ 1 (n + 12) = σ 1 n + 12

/-- A number $n$ comes from a prime quadruple $(p, p+2, p+6, p+8)$ if
$n = p(p+8)$ for some prime $p$ where $p$, $p+2$, $p+6$, $p+8$ are all prime. -/
def ComesFromPrimeQuadruple (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ (p + 2).Prime ∧ (p + 6).Prime ∧ (p + 8).Prime ∧ n = p * (p + 8)

/-- $65$ is in the sequence A56777. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_65 : A 65 := by
  refine ⟨?_, by norm_num, ?_, ?_⟩
  · simp only [show (65 : ℕ) = 5 * 13 by norm_num]
    exact not_prime_mul (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
  · decide
  · decide

/-- $209$ is in the sequence A56777. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_209 : A 209 := by
  unfold A
  simp only [one_lt_ofNat, reduceAdd, true_and]
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · norm_num
  · have eq1 : 221 = 13 * 17 := by norm_num
    have eq2 : 209 = 11 * 19 := by norm_num
    rw [eq1, eq2, totient_mul (by norm_num), totient_mul (by norm_num),
      totient_prime (by norm_num), totient_prime (by norm_num), totient_prime (by norm_num),
      totient_prime (by norm_num)]
  · decide

/-- Numbers coming from prime quadruples are in the sequence A56777. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
theorem a_of_comesFromPrimeQuadruple {n : ℕ} (h : ComesFromPrimeQuadruple n) : A n := by
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hp2, hp6, hp8, rfl⟩ := h
  -- n + 12 = p * (p+8) + 12 = (p+2) * (p+6)
  have hsum : p * (p + 8) + 12 = (p + 2) * (p + 6) := by ring
  -- coprimality facts between the four primes
  have hne_p_p8 : p ≠ p + 8 := by omega
  have hne_p2_p6 : p + 2 ≠ p + 6 := by omega
  have hcop1 : Nat.Coprime p (p + 8) := (Nat.coprime_primes hp hp8).mpr hne_p_p8
  have hcop2 : Nat.Coprime (p + 2) (p + 6) := (Nat.coprime_primes hp2 hp6).mpr hne_p2_p6
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  -- ¬ Prime (p * (p+8))
  · exact Nat.not_prime_mul hp.one_lt.ne' (by have := hp8.one_lt; omega)
  -- 1 < p * (p+8)
  · have h1 : 2 ≤ p := hp.two_le
    have h2 : 10 ≤ p + 8 := by omega
    nlinarith
  -- totient: φ((p+2)(p+6)) = φ(p(p+8)) + 12
  · rw [hsum, Nat.totient_mul hcop2, Nat.totient_mul hcop1,
        Nat.totient_prime hp, Nat.totient_prime hp2,
        Nat.totient_prime hp6, Nat.totient_prime hp8]
    zify [show 1 ≤ p from hp.one_lt.le, show 1 ≤ p + 2 by omega,
          show 1 ≤ p + 6 by omega, show 1 ≤ p + 8 by omega]
    ring
  -- sigma: σ₁((p+2)(p+6)) = σ₁(p(p+8)) + 12
  · rw [hsum, ArithmeticFunction.isMultiplicative_sigma.map_mul_of_coprime hcop2,
        ArithmeticFunction.isMultiplicative_sigma.map_mul_of_coprime hcop1]
    have e1 : ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1 p = p + 1 := by
      have := ArithmeticFunction.sigma_one_apply_prime_pow (p := p) (i := 1) hp
      simpa using this
    have e2 : ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1 (p + 2) = (p + 2) + 1 := by
      have := ArithmeticFunction.sigma_one_apply_prime_pow (p := p + 2) (i := 1) hp2
      simpa using this
    have e6 : ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1 (p + 6) = (p + 6) + 1 := by
      have := ArithmeticFunction.sigma_one_apply_prime_pow (p := p + 6) (i := 1) hp6
      simpa using this
    have e8 : ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1 (p + 8) = (p + 8) + 1 := by
      have := ArithmeticFunction.sigma_one_apply_prime_pow (p := p + 8) (i := 1) hp8
      simpa using this
    rw [e1, e2, e6, e8]
    ring

/-- $11009$ is in the sequence A56777. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_11009 : A 11009 := by
  apply a_of_comesFromPrimeQuadruple
  exact ⟨101, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by rfl⟩

/-- All members of the sequence A56777 come from prime quadruples. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem comesFromPrimeQuadruple_of_a {n : ℕ} (h : A n) : ComesFromPrimeQuadruple n := by
  sorry

/-- Numbers coming from prime quadruples satisfy $n \equiv 65 \pmod{72}$. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
theorem mod_72_of_comesFromPrimeQuadruple {n : ℕ} (h : ComesFromPrimeQuadruple n) :
    n % 72 = 65 := by
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hp2, hp6, hp8, rfl⟩ := h
  have hp5 : 5 ≤ p := by
    by_contra! hlt
    interval_cases p <;> simp_all (config := { decide := true })
  have h2 : ¬ (2 ∣ p) := by
    intro hdvd; cases hp.eq_one_or_self_of_dvd 2 hdvd with | inl h => omega | inr h => omega
  have h3 : ¬ (3 ∣ p) := by
    intro hdvd; cases hp.eq_one_or_self_of_dvd 3 hdvd with | inl h => omega | inr h => omega
  have hmod2 : p % 2 = 1 := by omega
  have hmod3 : p % 3 = 2 := by
    have hne1 : p % 3 ≠ 1 := by
      intro heq
      have h3dvd : 3 ∣ (p + 2) := ⟨p / 3 + 1, by omega⟩
      cases hp2.eq_one_or_self_of_dvd 3 h3dvd with | inl h => omega | inr h => omega
    omega
  have hmod6 : p % 6 = 5 := by omega
  set q := p / 6
  have hp_eq : p = 6 * q + 5 := by omega
  have hparity : 2 ∣ q * (q + 3) := by
    rcases Nat.even_or_odd q with ⟨r, hr⟩ | ⟨r, hr⟩
    · exact dvd_mul_of_dvd_left ⟨r, by omega⟩ _
    · exact dvd_mul_of_dvd_right ⟨r + 2, by omega⟩ _
  obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := hparity
  have h1 : p * (p + 8) = (6 * q + 5) * (6 * q + 13) := by congr 1; omega
  have h2 : (6 * q + 5) * (6 * q + 13) = 36 * (q * (q + 3)) + 65 := by ring
  have h3 : 36 * (q * (q + 3)) = 72 * k := by linarith
  have hprod : p * (p + 8) = 72 * k + 65 := by linarith
  omega

/-- Numbers coming from prime quadruples satisfy $n \equiv 9 \pmod{100}$,
except the first value "65". -/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
theorem mod_100_of_comesFromPrimeQuadruple {n : ℕ} (h65 : 65 < n) (h : ComesFromPrimeQuadruple n) :
    n % 100 = 9 := by
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hp2, hp6, hp8, rfl⟩ := h
  have hp5 : 5 ≤ p := by
    by_contra hlt; push Not at hlt
    interval_cases p <;> simp_all (config := { decide := true })
  have h2 : ¬ (2 ∣ p) := by
    intro hdvd; cases hp.eq_one_or_self_of_dvd 2 hdvd with | inl h => omega | inr h => omega
  have h3 : ¬ (3 ∣ p) := by
    intro hdvd; cases hp.eq_one_or_self_of_dvd 3 hdvd with | inl h => omega | inr h => omega
  have h5 : ¬ (5 ∣ p) := by
    intro hdvd; cases hp.eq_one_or_self_of_dvd 5 hdvd with | inl h => omega | inr h =>
      -- p = 5 → p*(p+8) = 65, but 65 < n = p*(p+8) is impossible
      subst h; omega
  have hmod30 : p % 30 = 11 := by
    have hmod2 : p % 2 = 1 := by omega
    have hmod3 : p % 3 = 2 := by
      have : p % 3 ≠ 1 := by
        intro heq; have : 3 ∣ (p + 2) := ⟨p / 3 + 1, by omega⟩
        cases hp2.eq_one_or_self_of_dvd 3 this with | inl h => omega | inr h => omega
      omega
    have hmod5 : p % 5 = 1 := by
      have hne2 : p % 5 ≠ 2 := by
        intro heq; have : 5 ∣ (p + 8) := ⟨p / 5 + 2, by omega⟩
        cases hp8.eq_one_or_self_of_dvd 5 this with | inl h => omega | inr h => omega
      have hne3 : p % 5 ≠ 3 := by
        intro heq; have : 5 ∣ (p + 2) := ⟨p / 5 + 1, by omega⟩
        cases hp2.eq_one_or_self_of_dvd 5 this with | inl h => omega | inr h => omega
      have hne4 : p % 5 ≠ 4 := by
        intro heq; have : 5 ∣ (p + 6) := ⟨p / 5 + 2, by omega⟩
        cases hp6.eq_one_or_self_of_dvd 5 this with | inl h => omega | inr h => omega
      omega
    omega
  set q := p / 30
  have hp_eq : p = 30 * q + 11 := by omega
  -- p*(p+8) = (30q+11)(30q+19) = 900*q*(q+1) + 30*(11+19)*q + 209
  -- = 900*q*(q+1) + 900*q + 209 ... let me just compute with ring
  have hparity : 2 ∣ q * (q + 1) := by
    rcases Nat.even_or_odd q with ⟨r, hr⟩ | ⟨r, hr⟩
    · exact dvd_mul_of_dvd_left ⟨r, by omega⟩ _
    · exact dvd_mul_of_dvd_right ⟨r + 1, by omega⟩ _
  obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := hparity
  have h1 : p * (p + 8) = (30 * q + 11) * (30 * q + 19) := by congr 1; omega
  have h2 : (30 * q + 11) * (30 * q + 19) = 900 * (q * (q + 1)) + 209 := by ring
  have h3 : 900 * (q * (q + 1)) = 1800 * k := by linarith
  have hprod : p * (p + 8) = 1800 * k + 209 := by linarith
  omega

end OeisA56777

findings.description: The module docstring's title is `# Divisibility of $2^n + 1$ by $n$`. A056777 has nothing to do with $2^n+1$. It is the sequence of composite $n$ with $\varphi(n+12)=\varphi(n)+12$ and $\sigma(n+12)=\sigma(n)+12$, and no declaration in the file mentions $2^n+1$. The rest of the module docstring describes the sequence correctly. The local git history shows the title came from the bulk retitling in commit d16e05a (#4384, "add solutions from AlphaProof Nexus"). That commit replaced the original `# Conjectures associated with A56777` with what looks like a title meant for a different sequence (numbers n dividing 2^n+1). The mathematics of the file is unaffected.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A056777, %N line: "Composite numbers k such that both phi(k+12) = phi(k) + 12 and sigma(k+12) = sigma(k) + 12." (read from the official OEIS data mirror, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A056/A056777.seq, rev. #28 of Jun 13 2026; the same wording appears in the 2023 Wayback snapshot of https://oeis.org/A056777).
findings.suggested_fix: Retitle the module docstring, e.g. `# Composite numbers $n$ with $\varphi(n+12) = \varphi(n) + 12$ and $\sigma(n+12) = \sigma(n) + 12$`.

findings.description: The declaration is true, proved in the file, matches its own docstring, and is correctly tagged `textbook`. The concern is coverage. It is the file's only rendering of A056777's congruence observation, and it states the congruence only for prime-quadruple numbers p(p+8), which makes it an elementary fact. The source's claim concerns all terms of the sequence, and the source now calls it a conjecture. No declaration states `∀ n, A n → n % 72 = 65`. That claim is strictly weaker than `comesFromPrimeQuadruple_of_a` and is itself still open. The file captures it only conditionally: I checked in Lean that `fun _ h => mod_72_of_comesFromPrimeQuadruple (comesFromPrimeQuadruple_of_a h)` proves it from the sorry'd main conjecture. Yet the module docstring says the conjectures cover "congruences satisfied by the members of A56777". This is a defensible modelling choice (the file's author wrote the OEIS comment), but it drops an open problem that the source poses.
findings.source_evidence: A056777 comments: "Numbers so far are all congruent to 65 (mod 72). - Ralf Stephan, Jul 07 2003" and "The conjecture that all terms arise from prime quadruplets, and that all terms are congruent to 65 (mod 72), has been verified up to 10^12. - Himaghna Roy Choudhury, Jun 05 2026" (oeisdata seq/A056/A056777.seq, rev. #28).
findings.suggested_fix: Add an open statement for all terms, e.g. `/-- "Numbers so far are all congruent to 65 (mod 72)." (Ralf Stephan) -/ @[category research open, AMS 11] theorem mod_72_of_a {n : ℕ} (h : A n) : n % 72 = 65 := by sorry`; I checked that this compiles. Also reword the module docstring to say the congruences are proved for prime-quadruple numbers and conjectured for all terms.

reformulations.difference: The docstring says "except the first value 65", but the Lean hypothesis is `65 < n`, not `n ≠ 65`. The congruence n ≡ 9 (mod 100) also does not appear in the A056777 entry in any revision: not #16 (Dec 2021, current when the file was written) and not #28 (Jun 2026). It is an elementary fact added by the formalizer. It follows from A007530's comment "Except for the first term, 5, all terms == 11 (mod 30)".
reformulations.equivalence_argument: If n = p(p+8) with p, p+2, p+6, p+8 all prime, then p ≥ 5 (p = 2 and p = 3 fail), so n ≥ 65. Under `ComesFromPrimeQuadruple n`, `65 < n ↔ n ≠ 65` therefore holds; I proved this in a scratch file. The statement itself is true: for p > 5, p ≡ 11 (mod 30), so p(p+8) = (30q+11)(30q+19) ≡ 209 (mod 1800). The file proves it without sorry (axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound).

sources_consulted: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/72c53dd50967ac7166f7d31bf79be95174ec5bc6/seq/A056/A056777.seq (rev. #16, Dec 2021: the version current when the Lean file was written in Jan 2026)
review.notes:
The Lean mathematics of every declaration is correct. Both findings concern documentation or coverage, not a wrong statement.

Checks:
- `A` matches OEIS %N exactly: `¬n.Prime ∧ 1 < n` means composite, `Nat.totient`, and `σ 1` = ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1, confirmed with #print. The OEIS PARI code uses `!isprime(n)`, which would admit n = 1, but n = 0 and n = 1 fail the φ equation anyway, so nothing changes.
- A perl sieve up to 10^6 finds exactly the non-prime solutions 65, 209, 11009, 38009, 680609. A Lean `#eval` of `A` on n < 1200 gives [65, 209]. All 166 b-file terms (up to about 9.7·10^11) have the form p(p+8) with p, p+2, p+6, p+8 prime, are ≡ 65 (mod 72), and, except 65, are ≡ 9 (mod 100).
- `ComesFromPrimeQuadruple` and `a_of_comesFromPrimeQuadruple` match McCranie's \"easy to show\" claim; the latter is textbook and proved.
- `comesFromPrimeQuadruple_of_a` matches McCranie's conjecture, \"all members of the sequence are of this form\". It is correctly tagged `research open`: OEIS rev. #28 (June 2026) records only computational verification up to 10^12, and I found no proof or counterexample. I ran no successful literature search (the arXiv API returned nothing and web search gave irrelevant results), so the status rests on the OEIS entry.
- `mod_72_of_comesFromPrimeQuadruple`, `mod_100_of_comesFromPrimeQuadruple` and the three `test` theorems are all proved, with axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Only `comesFromPrimeQuadruple_of_a` depends on sorryAx.

Access:
- The oeis.org HTML pages returned a Cloudflare challenge. I read the entry through the official OEIS data repository (oeisdata), the b-file (which was reachable) and a 2023 Wayback snapshot.
- I used the local git history of the checkout only to trace where the wrong title came from (commit d16e05a, #4384) and to see which OEIS revision the file was written against. I did not use GitHub for formal-conjectures.
- `git diff` shows a lakefile.toml change adding `Challenge` and `Solution` libraries. It was there before I started and is not mine; the file under review is unmodified at aea251bb.
